senses.definition: to repeal or do away with a law, right or formal agreement
senses.example: The new government abrogated the trade treaty.

senses.definition: to reduce the force, effect or value of something
senses.example: The thick walls attenuate the noise from the street.

senses.definition: puzzled, confused or bewildered
senses.example: She gave a bemused look at the strange menu.

senses.definition: to remove material considered improper or offensive from a text, especially with the result that it becomes weaker
senses.example: The publisher bowdlerized the novel for younger readers.

senses.definition: continually finding fault in a petty way
senses.example: He was weary of his boss's carping comments.

senses.definition: severely critical of others
senses.example: Her censorious neighbors disapproved of everything she did.

senses.definition: to think deeply about something; to meditate or reflect
senses.example: He sat on the bench, cogitating on what to do next.

senses.definition: to act or move slowly
senses.example: Don't dally on your way home from school.

senses.definition: to have a casual romantic or sexual liaison with someone, or to take a casual interest in something
senses.example: He dallied with the idea of becoming a painter.

senses.definition: to tear something up by the roots; to uproot
senses.example: War deracinated whole communities.

senses.definition: a state of disuse
senses.example: The old rail line fell into desuetude after the war.

senses.definition: (especially of fabric) light, delicate and translucent
senses.example: The dancer wore a diaphanous silk scarf.

senses.definition: slow to act
senses.example: The council was dilatory in fixing the roads.

senses.definition: intended to cause delay
senses.example: The defense used dilatory tactics to postpone the trial.

senses.definition: to persuade someone that an idea or belief is mistaken
senses.example: Let me disabuse you of the idea that this job will be easy.

senses.definition: dissatisfied with the people in authority and no longer willing to support them
senses.example: The party tried to win back disaffected voters.

senses.definition: comic verse composed in irregular rhythm
senses.example: The birthday card was full of cheerful doggerel.

senses.definition: to establish or settle someone in a comfortable, safe or secret place
senses.example: She ensconced herself in an armchair with a novel.

senses.definition: smelling extremely unpleasant
senses.example: The fetid water in the ditch was full of flies.

senses.definition: to express vehement protest
senses.example: He fulminated against the new parking rules.

senses.definition: relevant to a subject under consideration
senses.example: Her experience abroad was germane to the new job.

senses.definition: denoting a period of time in the past that was idyllically happy and peaceful
senses.example: She remembered the halcyon days of her childhood on the farm.

senses.definition: not honorable in character or purpose
senses.example: He refused to stoop to such ignoble tactics.

senses.definition: an extremely confused, complicated or embarrassing situation
senses.example: The minister was caught in a diplomatic imbroglio.

senses.definition: failing to possess or display prudence; unwise
senses.example: It would be impolitic to criticize the boss in public.

senses.definition: to ask someone pressingly and persistently for or to do something
senses.example: The beggars importuned every tourist who passed.

senses.definition: to imply or hint
senses.example: He intimated that he might resign.

senses.definition: closely acquainted; familiar
senses.example: They were intimate friends for forty years.

words.note: As a verb, intimate means to hint.

senses.definition: reluctant; unwilling
senses.example: She was loath to leave the warm house.

words.note: Loath means unwilling; loathe is the verb meaning to hate.

senses.definition: sentimental in an exaggerated or false way
senses.example: The film's mawkish ending spoiled an otherwise honest story.

senses.definition: insisting on immediate attention or obedience, especially in a brusquely imperious way
senses.example: The boss gave a peremptory order to leave the room.

senses.definition: deceitfulness; untrustworthiness
senses.example: The general's perfidy cost the king his crown.

senses.definition: petty; worthless
senses.example: The committee wasted hours on picayune details.

senses.definition: an expression of praise or approval
senses.example: The novel won plaudits from critics.

senses.definition: lacking in refinement
senses.example: His plebeian tastes amused his snobbish in-laws.

senses.definition: a member of the lower social classes
senses.example: In ancient Rome, plebeians could not marry patricians.

senses.definition: to be a sign or warning that something, typically something bad, will happen
senses.example: The dark clouds presaged a storm.

senses.definition: a sign or warning that something will happen; an omen
senses.example: The warm winter was a presage of drought.

senses.definition: giving or indicating a good chance of success; favorable
senses.example: It was a propitious moment to launch the business.

senses.definition: beauty
senses.example: The poems celebrate the pulchritude of the countryside.

senses.definition: complaining in a petulant or whining manner
senses.example: The querulous patient found fault with every meal.

senses.definition: to argue or raise objections about a trivial matter
senses.example: They quibbled over the cost of the coffee.

senses.definition: a slight objection or criticism
senses.example: My only quibble with the book is its length.

senses.definition: stubborn or unmanageable
senses.example: The refractory mule refused to move.

senses.definition: (of a disease) not yielding to treatment
senses.example: The doctors tried a new drug on refractory cases.

senses.definition: such as to provoke laughter
senses.example: The idea that he could run a marathon was risible.

senses.definition: relating to tailoring, clothes or style of dress
senses.example: He was known for his sartorial elegance.

senses.definition: extreme preoccupation with and indulgence of one's feelings and desires; egoistic self-absorption
senses.example: The memoir's solipsism grows tiresome.

senses.definition: the view or theory that the self is all that can be known to exist
senses.example: The philosophy course began with a debate on solipsism.

senses.definition: to stop or restrict the flow of something
senses.example: Doctors struggled to stem the bleeding.

senses.definition: to originate in or be caused by
senses.example: His anger stems from years of neglect.

words.note: Besides meaning to arise from, stem means to stop or restrain.

senses.definition: a person who is self-indulgent in their fondness for sensuous luxury
senses.example: The sybarite spent his days in silk robes eating sweets.

senses.definition: equivalent in seriousness to; virtually the same as
senses.example: Staying silent would be tantamount to lying.

senses.definition: expressing or intending to promote a particular cause or point of view, especially a controversial one
senses.example: The documentary was criticized as tendentious.

senses.definition: (of language or style) tediously pompous or bombastic
senses.example: The novel's turgid prose makes it hard to finish.

senses.definition: swollen and distended or congested
senses.example: The river was turgid after the rains.

senses.definition: to find fault with someone; to scold
senses.example: The captain upbraided the crew for their carelessness.

senses.definition: having or showing a lack of thought or intelligence; mindless
senses.example: The show was vacuous entertainment.

senses.definition: relating to deep inward feelings rather than to the intellect
senses.example: He had a visceral dislike of the man.

senses.definition: to use flattery or coaxing in order to persuade someone to do something or give one something
senses.example: The child wheedled an extra cookie out of her grandmother.
